“No, I’m not a rake.” He smiled, and his eyes didn’t meet hers as he turned to lay on his back, his face to the ceiling. She noticed the tips of his pointed ears flushed pink.

He didn’t elaborate, so she stopped pushing the subject.

She took the opportunity to look at him as he stared elsewhere and wondered if he’d ever been with anyone. Ilya clearly loved him; the girls in Gerudo Town would have lined up to let him have his way with them. And every time she walked next to him in the castle, girls and women would turn and fawn over him. He wouldn’t even have to try; a handsome, lean, strong, honorable knight. Of course, everyone swooned at the sight of him.

Surely he’s… indulged… at some point, with someone. Perhaps not with the aforementioned but with someone over his twenty years of living.

Thinking about him in that position with a faceless woman. She imagined his calloused hands gently undoing every button of a shirt or every lace of a corset. He was probably strategic yet swift in his movements as he was in battle. His large hands tugging the clothing up and over, and tracing every curve, every inch of skin as he freed her of her clothing. He would be able to lift her with ease, guiding her body wherever he desired. His lips hungrily devouring her lips, her jaw, her neck. Her body reacting to his touch, aching for him, slick with desire. How his trousers would stiff with want for her, and she’d free him of his confines to be greeted by a perfect velvet member. His corded muscles flexing, expelling little effort, against a wall, or a bed, or a tent—

“Zelda? Are you alright?”

She was embarrassingly snapped out of her thoughts with a shaky gasp. He looked at her with such earnest concern as her thumb had somehow ended up in her mouth nibbling her own flesh thinking about him. She tried to hide the obvious flush and desire that was written all over her face and squirming body. She calmed herself discreetly, hoping he couldn’t see her core had become liquid at the thought of him. 

“Yes” she squeaked, “I’m alright; it’s just… hot in here.”

Thankfully, the rain had started, and they both lay quietly, listening to the sounds of frogs singing and water pelting the fabric of the tent. The air had become cool and breezy, giving her a much-needed reprieve. She snuck a peek at Link, his eyes still open, staring at the ceiling.

“I loved camping as a child,” she started, her voice low and muffled by the sounds of rain on the tent. He turned his attention to her, his blue eyes fixed on her mouth as she turned her face to the ceiling, not able to look at him as she continued. The smells of the rain sparking that memory.

“My parents and I would go any chance we could. It was my favorite thing to do with them. We would go every year during the spring, then summer, then again in the fall as the leaves turned colors and the crisp air greeted us each morning. After the long winter, I’d always look forward to our trip in the spring, just when it started to get warm and the flowers bloomed and their strong scents filled our noses.” She had been smiling fondly at those memories, and her smile faded and  she bravely swallowed that building hurt in her throat, “Then after they died, I stopped going. Until now, with you.” She said softly.

”I’m sorry.” Link turned his whole body to her as he breathed, “What happened to them?”

She swallowed, “It was in the summer after my birthday. I had just turned eighteen, and we went out to dinner. On the way back, we were driving.” She paused to articulate, “Driving is basically carts that you have but you sit in them, encased. It’s powered by energy rather than horses and can go much, much faster than horses.” He nodded his head in understanding. “Anyway, we were driving home, and something darted out in front of the car, a deer or elk or something large and unavoidable. My father swerved out of the way, but he lost control and slammed into a tree. It was a horrible crash. Both my parents died almost instantly, while I had not a scratch on me in the backseat.”

Link was silent, just staring at her, waiting for her to continue.

She was rubbing her hands, fidgeting with her golden triangle ring, the last and only piece of jewelry from her mother. She curled her lip. “It’s ironic because I thought I would go the same way. Something darted in front of my car. I lost control and hit a tree. Except I ended up here, the day you found me.” She choked back that rising cry to continue, but she couldn’t help her voice falter a bit. “After I came here and the initial shock wore off, a quick creeping thought entered my mind: that maybe I’d see them again. Maybe that they were here too. But they aren’t.”

She remembered that she buried them in the earth, she saw their bodies lower into the ground. Whereas she was here.

A silent tear escaped down her cheek as she whispered, nose flaring “I miss them. They were wonderful people. Not just because they were my parents, but because they were inherently good.”

They were good, the best. Not only her harbor, her safe place, but they were her home. It was why she couldn’t stay in her childhood home after it happened. They left her everything in their will: the materialistic items, the now-wrecked car, and their home. She walked in and collapsed in their bedroom and hadn’t been able to move, a loss so deep that a part of her died while she still held breath in her lungs. The house was no longer a home without them in it. So she sold it, and everything inside it, and moved into Marin’s the next week.

“I know the feeling.” He said in a sad tone.

“What happened?” She managed to turn towards him, her eyes still lined with silver.

He faced her, but his eyes drifted elsewhere as he told the story, “My father was a knight. He was well respected and liked by everyone. He would be stationed in certain regions or would be called away if needed all throughout his career. When I had become a page, he was called away to a small village that was having issues with a group of monsters attacking their crops and livestock. He was outnumbered when he arrived, but he didn’t flee. He—” his voice faltered, the same way her own did as she watched him swallow, hard, “—he died protecting them, saving them, and their village.”

“I’m sorry.” She whispered.

He continued, “And my mother loved my father, and he loved her. They actually chose each other, no arrangements, just true love. When he died, she was devastatingly heartbroken, she ended up dying a year later from illness, but I think her broken heart weakened her, making her susceptible to catching something.” His jaw was tight as he finished. Pain behind his eyes.

The tears Zelda held in earlier at retelling her own story now slowly fell on her cheeks in hot streaks. They were facing each other, so intimately in this closed space, sharing the darkest depths of their souls, scars visible that were deep and ugly.

She looked at this man she’d spent so much time with these past few months. It was the first time she looked past his beautiful features, not through him, but into him. How much they still didn’t know about each other. How his need for perfection probably stemmed from his father’s death. Or his unwillingness to love to avoid his mother’s fate.

Just as her own weaknesses manifested with her parents’ death. Dreams she had led way to the guilt. Her optimism faded and was replaced with isolation.

She inhaled a deep breath, the air burning her nostrils raw. “I’m so sorry, Link.” She reached for his hand and curled her fingers around his. He returned it with a soft grip, his calloused hands rough against her soft fingers.

“I’m sorry too, Zelda.”

They sat in comfortable silence as the rain stopped and the insects resumed their songs, and somewhere in between, she closed her eyes and drifted off to sleep.

Ironically, it was one of the best nights of sleep she had in as long as she could remember.

Chapter 21: Tavern
Chapter Text
He had slept the best he had in a long time.

He woke, facing Zelda. She was soft and peaceful; her golden hair long and loose tangled around her shoulder, her eyelashes long, sweeping her cheeks. Her breathing was slow and steady. 

He didn’t want to get used to it.

When she invited him into her tent, he was tense, unwilling to immediately say yes. He wasn’t sure he could manage spending the night so close to her. He certainly didn’t want to endure the cold rain pelting his face, but she persisted until he couldn’t think of any more legitimate excuses to give her.

Then he when he entered, he was hit with her lavender scent. It was intoxicating. He was so close to her. He tried to lay as far as he could to give her space, to give himself space, but no matter how close he got to the edge, they were barely an arm’s length away from each other.

He eyed the hem of the white silk nightdress that fell just above her knee, leaving her legs bare. It was the one that was opaque and hugged her like a second skin. The same white silk dress he had caught her in on her balcony so long ago. The same dress he had fantasized her wearing when he pictured her behind her apartment door. Despite the large sweater she wore covering most of her, he steeled his whole body, staring straight at the ceiling, for fear that if he looked at her, he would combust.

Then she brought up courting, marriage, and sex. He willed every part of training ever given to him to not physically react. He was tightly fisting his hand, so much so he was sure he was doing irreparable damage to his sword arm.

Thoughts of her with another man kept him in check, if not twisted him. She had said she didn’t date often, but thinking of someone else caressing her soft skin, tugging on her hair, claiming her with their mouth, tasting her—  it was unpleasant to picture. Even if she had every right to choose to be with anyone she wanted, even if it wasn’t him.

He was content with only being able to admire her from a distance, only fantasizing about the possibilities of having her, never imagining it could become a reality. However, it was becoming increasingly challenging as of late for him to confine himself to only his fantasies, especially as he watched her fidgeting beside him. She was biting her finger, her pupils grew large, her chest swelled as her gaze trailed from his legs to her torso. He almost reached his hand to her face, to slide behind her neck, pull her on top of him, taste her.

But he didn’t.

Then the rain came, and it was as if a cold shower symbolically ran over him. Grounding him. He thought about sitting in his hammock to cool off, but she changed the subject to her parents.

He never asked her about them before because she never brought it up, or would purposely avoid it if the subject came close. He recognized the deflection tactics, because he did the same. And after their journey back from the Gerudo Desert, she spoke of her best friend Linda, her adult guardian figure who also happened to be her landlord, Marin, but not a word about her parents. But last night, she opened up to him, raw and honest, and he felt open to reciprocate her sentiment and share his own darkness, which he had never done.

Everyone in the military knew of his father; he was known to be an extremely honorable knight. He served in the castle guard at a young age, then met his mother, moved to Hateno, and was assigned to regional posts. He would be away from his family for months at a time, but often got the same amount of time off to spend with them.

And his mother... besides the obvious; lovely, beautiful, and graceful. She was giving and kind. But not to be taken as meek, never known to be submissive. She was tough without ever having to pick up a sword or spear in her life. Her sharp wit was her blade, only used sparingly, typically when needing to keep him and his father in check.

And because of his two wonderful parents, he had a happy childhood, as she seemed to have, but there was now forever a hole in his heart that could never be repaired. He buried that emptiness deep within himself to never think about it. Not even Ilya brought them up to him, as she saw how he became distant and cold when she did.

Zelda and he shared something most others couldn’t relate to. They had no blood left in this world.

At least he hadn’t watched his parents die in front of him. He couldn’t imagine that type of pain carved into her own heart.

Despite the heaviness of the conversation, he felt light the next morning. He crept out of the tent, careful not to disturb her sleeping form. The storm had passed, leaving behind a warm rolling fog, despite the crisp winter air. He prepared breakfast and practiced his daily drills under a swirl of an orange and blue sky, the warmth from the sun beating down on him. He leaned into training his other hand because his arm with his wound still ached something fierce. He mused that it was good practice; knights should be adept at both anyway.

She awoke a bit later, greeting him with a bright smile, and he remembered why he wanted to reach for her the night before.

She was daylight in human form.

Their trip back was light and breezy. They took their time and enjoyed the scenery, which he rarely appreciated anymore. He had forgotten the beauty that Hyrule had to offer, now watching Zelda appreciate every blade of grass or picturesque landscape. It was as if he was seeing it for the first time along with her, remembering why he loved the wilds as he did. He watched her pick flowers when they stopped, a bouquet of pink, purple and blue winter flowers and the feeling he felt watching her was indefinable, as if it was a new seedling begging for that light, clawing it’s way up from the abyss within him. Whatever it was, he knew he wanted to hold on to it.

She made him want to live. Not just to exist. He’d forgotten what magic the land offered. He only ever planned one path in his life: become a royal guard knight, protect the princess, die a hero. Walk that narrow parapet, any deviation meant plummeting failure. Be the mindless drone. Don’t question. Enjoyment is secondary. Don’t partake in fun, don’t— love.

He never considered another possibility here, perhaps because it wasn’t originally present. It was elsewhere.

As they trotted into the west side of Castle Town, his mind was flooded with these new revelations, he was distracted by it until he started leading Epona into the water reservoir instead, and she nickered her displeasure, much to Zelda’s delight.

After they arrived to their apartments, before shutting her door to unpack and rest, she reminded him that he owed her a drink, as he promised. He left her after trying and failing, to conceal a wide smile and agreeing to fetch her at sundown. They would grab supper and drinks in Castle Town at the tavern.

He spent the majority of the day packing for their upcoming trip to Zora’s Domain. They would leave tomorrow or the day after, depending on the weather. The mountainous path, though not far from the castle, would drain their stamina as they hiked around the river. If they maintained a steady pace, he estimated a solid two days of travel. But he wouldn’t mind if it took longer; spending time with Zelda outside the castle, really anywhere, was preferable compared to anything else.

Trying to distract himself, he thought of Mipha, his old childhood friend. Like Ilya, he’d grown up with Mipha when his father was stationed in Zora’s Domain. He learned how to swim from her, and he taught her how to shoot a bow and arrow. 

It had been a while since he had seen her, it had been at the Din Solstice Ball at the castle. As with every major celebration or event, every region in Hyrule sent its royalty or leaders to participate. Mipha was escorted by her father, while Link attended with Ilya. He was obligated to attend and bring a date as a high-ranking knight, to his dismay, so he asked Ilya, as he always had for those types of events.

But surely, word of the tournament and his appointment had reached the Domain by now. He was curious to know what his old friend would think of his task. And Zelda.

With the mere whisper of the thought of her, his mind drifted back to Zelda. It was getting increasingly hard every time he was near her not to be completely consumed by her. It was easier when they weren’t speaking, but now he was getting to know her, hearing her laugh, listening to her stories, learning about her life. He had continuously forgotten his assignment at hand: to get her home.

A pit grew in his stomach. Despite everything they had endured, she still wanted to return home. And he would likely never see her again.

The thought of never seeing her hazy smile after waking up in the morning, hearing her voice say “my knight,” the curious twinkle in her green eyes after she learned something about Hyrule or him…

Or never gaining the courage to tell her how he felt.

It was good timing that he was going to Zora’s Domain. He could spend some time with Mipha, try to get his head straight with a distraction.

Dusk had started to set. He decided to knock on her main door. Had he seen her in the threshold of their adjoining door, he would be too consumed by thoughts of wanting to pull her into his room instead.

He had bathed and combed his hair. He kept his red tunic on, sans guards, bracer, and belt. It was the nicer choice of clothes he owned, excluding his formal wear. In which he would not willingly wear out unless absolutely necessary.

After his third knock on her door, she opened to him. It was as if a Hinox punched him, the air escaping his lungs.

She was stunning, more than stunning. She wore a green linen skirt that flowed out to her feet. As a top, she was only wearing a white corset that enhanced her silhouette like an hourglass, with a casual slouching brown sweater hung over her pointed shoulders. Her hair was styled in a flowing braid to her side, which she decorated with flowers from their travels. She wore no rouge or eye stain as some women opted to do for going out. But she didn’t need it, she was naturally perfect.

 It wasn’t a particularly fancy or formal outfit; it actually was quite plain compared to the fashion of the time, but she could make rags look formal. He wasn’t sure to curse Impa or thank her for the clothing she provided Zelda.

“Link? Is this okay?”

He wasn’t paying attention; he drawled back to her eyes, which matched her skirt. 

“You look amazing.” He managed to spit out.

She smiled at the compliment, her cheek bones round, eyes gleaming. “And you don’t look so bad yourself. I see you went with a different outfit this time.”

He rolled his eyes at her joke.

“Well, if you look good in something, might as well wear it often.” She drawled and smirked.

Had she complimented him? He suddenly felt hot.

“Shall we, my lady?” He exaggerated his tone and held his arm out for her to grab. She huffed a laugh and slid her arm through. Lavender filled his senses as they walked down towards town, happily recounting how they spent their time apart to each other. It was so easy.

They made it to the Mercay Tavern a half hour later. This tavern was the most reputable in town, very unlike the one Zelda had stumbled into her first night outside of the castle. Castle staff, respected knights, and soldiers would often frequent this establishment, as it was better known for good food, drinks, and more often entertainment. Link escorted her inside, and they found the room to be dark and loud, it was full of everyone in castle town. He scanned the packed room and, to his dismay, no tables were open; they would have to wait, and he kicked himself at not having the foresight to arrive earlier.

“Link!” A familiar voice said from across the room.

It was Fledge, waving him over. He had managed to be sitting at a booth near the stage but still somewhat private.

It wasn’t exactly how he wanted his night with Zelda to go, but better than having to stand and wait.

When they arrived at the table, Fledge hadn’t been alone. Link was startled to see Groose sitting next to him; surprise painted his features. “Groose, it’s good to see you.”

Groose stood and his large frame towered over both of them as he extended his hand in greeting.

“Groose, this is Zelda. My charge. She’s Ilya’s cousin.” He continued that lie. The fewer people that know the truth, the better.

Groose turned to her and smiled, his hazel eyes wide and sincere, “It’s lovely to meet you, Zelda. Fledge has told me about you.”

Link eyed Fledge curiously, but Fledge was faintly shaking his head. He had not told Groose the full truth.

“It’s a pleasure to meet you, Sir Groose.” Zelda said as both were ushered to sit down.

They all sat in awkward silence after the introductions. Link hadn’t imagined seeing Groose here. They hadn’t spoken since before the tournament that decided their fates.

Zelda seemed to pick up on that and decidedly broke the tension. “You were able to get the night off, Sir Groose?”

He looked slightly surprised, “Uh, yes. I usually have most nights off. There’s a guard stationed outside the Princess’s door each night. So unless we are traveling or I’m requested personally, I usually have my nights off.”

“How’s it been going with the Princess?” She continued, though stealing a glance at Link after she said it. Perhaps Zelda was curious what the possible fate had been if roles were reversed.

Groose was taken aback with the brazen line of Zelda’s questions, as he nervously scratched his flamboyant red hair, but he answered, “It’s been alright. We don’t speak much. She’s fairly quiet, has her routines, her studies. We’ve visited Goron City and Rito Village. She’s mostly intrigued by rumors of ancient technology and trying to sniff out where it might be buried.” Groose quickly looked around him as if someone was listening in. “Our Princess is very bookish.” He finished with a mumble.

Before Zelda could continue her grilling, the barmaid came to take their order. Zelda looked to Link for guidance on what was available.

He said to her quietly over the roar of the bar, “If you like chicken pot pie, they are known for it, and they have ales and various wines.”

“What are you getting?” She yelled-whispered back as Groose ordered.

“Chicken pot pie and an ale.”

The barmaid turned to her, “I’ll have a chicken pot pie and a Hyrule Ale, please.” 

“Same.” Link finished.

A short time later, the drinks and food arrived, and they began consuming them. Link had purposely slowed down his usual speed of eating to be polite. Zelda noticed and snickered. The food had been delicious as always, albeit slightly dry. Both Link and Zelda swiftly downed their ales and were ordering another soon after.

He had been impressed by Zelda’s tolerance and delight in the ale. They rarely had alcoholic beverages while traveling; most regions, except for the Gerudo, were not known for their variations of spirits. She seemed to read his thoughts.

“Don’t worry about me, I can handle my alcohol.” She gave him a wicked grin, and a twinkle shone in her eye.

“I have no doubt; enjoy yourself. It’s rare we get to partake.” As he brought his own mug to his lips.

She had her elbow on the table and rested her chin in her hand as she stared at him, “Why don’t we enjoy ourselves like this more often?”

He took another slow sip of his drink then said, “I don’t know; I don’t have a good explanation for that.”

“We should, if you want to. We haven’t gotten any solid leads in how to get me home, so what’s the rush?” She shrugged and swigged the remaining of her second ale. 

That was a loaded statement. Link wasn’t as thrilled at that as he should be. There was a hint of defeat in her tone. Like she was settling.

And that unsettled him.

Before he could think of something to say, the band had started to play a popular jig. She was holding her hand up for another round, and her head was swaying to the music. The famous traveling bard had returned to play in Castle Town again, likely why the tavern was packed.

Link had heard all about the bard but never seen him play. He didn’t even know his name. He was obviously of Sheikah descent, with white hair and red eyes, about his age, dressed in flamboyant garb with a lute in his hands. And as he strummed his lute, it was evident why the tavern was packed.

The four of them watched and listened attentively to the band. The bard had a pleasant singing voice, while the background players harmonized with violins, cellos, and drums. He looked over to Zelda, who looked so light and free, smiling and swaying her head in tune to the chorus. She caught his eye and smiled wider, before turning her attention back to the band. He nearly melted.

The band performed their first set, playing popular songs from across Hyrule, including regional tunes from Gerudo Town and Zora’s Domain. After a brief intermission, the bard laid down his lute, and as Link watched him he noticed that his gaze fell upon Zelda.

The bard was smiling suggestively at her as he made his way over to the table, his eyes never leaving hers.

“Good evening, my lady, good sirs.” He bowed his head and held his hand out to take Zelda’s hand to kiss it. Link seethed.

“You were wonderful.” Zelda smiled back at him. “I haven’t heard music so lovely in such a long time.”

“You flatter me, my lady. I but only play from my heart.” He held his hand above his heart and shot Zelda a toothy smile. “May I ask what your name is?”

“Zelda.” She said as she took a less than lady like sip of her ale.

His brows shot up. “You not only share our Princess’ name but also her beauty. Would you honor me with a dance?”

She raised her brow, “Aren’t you needed to play?”

“They can get on without me for one song— or two.” He winked. Link was sure his molars were going to crack.

She chanced a look at Link, awaiting some type of validation, but he didn’t give it before she turned back to the bard. “I would love to, it’s been a while since I’ve danced, so forgive me if I’m clumsy.”

“Nothing is sweeter than holding on to a lady, regardless of whether she’s good or bad at dancing.” He held his hand out to escort Zelda from the table. Zelda shot Link one more unknown look, and the charming bard whisked her away to the center of the dance floor.

The bard grabbed her hand and her waist as he pulled her into himself, and the band started to play. Link supposed he was handsome. Ilya made it clear on many occasions that the girls he associated with loved him. No wonder he would focus his attention on Zelda out of all the women around them. She was unmatched and radiated energy that had men gravitating to her.

The bard started to spin her, her skirt rising and flowing, as he flashed his perfect white teeth at her. Link sat and glared at them, never tearing his eyes away. It was only to protect her, if the need had arisen. He told himself that lie.

“You should ask her to dance afterwards.” Fledge murmured in the loud room.

“Why?” Link ground out.

He hadn’t bothered to look at Fledge, his glare still on the bard, but Fledge said simply, “Because she’ll say yes.”

Link hadn’t dared to think that. He had been so busy controlling his nerves and reactions every time he was near her that the last thing he thought to do was to embrace her. In public.

The song had ended. This was his moment: either be courageous and ask her or grit and bear it as the bard continued to hold her in all the ways he wanted to.

He rose from his chair, and before his brain could fully catch up, he was standing in front of them as the song finished.

“Zelda, may I have your next dance?” He held out his hand, willing himself not to clench it into a fist.

She tilted her head and her braid swayed. “But of course, honorable knight of mine.” She said with that hint of mockery only he recognized as she turned to the bard with a soft smile. “Thank you for the dance.”

He bowed his head to her, then shot Link an annoyed glare and made his way back to the stage.

Link took her hand in his and placed the other on the curve of her waist. She placed her hand on his shoulder as the music started to play. It was a steady song, so he set the pace, stepping out and back.

Her mouth fell open and brows furrowed in exaggerated shock. “How do you know how to dance?”

“Knights train in all courtly traditions, including dancing. Can’t have us embarrassing the royal family at royal balls where we are required to attend.” 

“I would have never guessed that.” She eyed him from feet to arms as he led her around in practiced motions. “You are quite good.” Her eyes landed on his chest. “I suppose there are a lot of things you’re good at that I’m unaware of.”

His heart skipped, he was sure she saw it under her gaze. “I can show you anything you want to see, anytime, if you’re curious.” He was feeling particularly cheeky, completely dazed by the proximity of her as he purred back, his eyes never leaving her own as she lifted them from his chest to lock onto.

A faint pink decorated her cheeks at the connection. “You’re quite bold tonight. Let’s see how you finish.” She had a wicked gleam in her eye in challenge.

He knew the song they were playing, so he held out for the perfect moment. As the bridge started its peak, he spun her outwards, extended her arm out with his. After she was fully extended, he pulled her back into his chest and held her back and dipped her, slowly, so slowly. She reached her free hand to press on his chest. As he held her low, his breath shaky, her eyes wide on him. If they weren’t in a room full of people, he would have kissed her right then.

He lifted her back up, her hand still firmly resting on his chest. She exhaled deeply. “Wow, your talents are wasted on being a knight.” Her eyes were wild gazing into his. She bit her lower lip. He resisted every urge to grab her face and taste her.

Before he could respond, the music stopped. He snuck a look at the bard, who looked positively murderous with him. A victorious feeling crept into his chest.

“Would you like to dance again?” She asked him.

“I’ll dance with you as long as you’ll have me.”

“That’s a tempting suggestion.” She smiled at him as the band started to play a slower song. Link knew this one as well.

He grabbed her waist and hand, this time closing the distance between them, so close he could feel her breath tickling his neck as she placed her chin on his shoulder. 

He recognized the faint plucks of the lute strings and harmonies of the violin and flute in the background as they slowly spun next to other couples that had joined around them. The melodies blanketed them and he thought he could do this with her forever.

He never enjoyed dancing, despite having years of lessons, he rarely danced at balls, unless Ilya or Mipha dragged him out and even then it was torture to have attention on him. Now, he hadn’t cared if there were a thousand eyes upon him.

But suddenly, she jerked her face backwards to meet his own, her body tense under his hands, her eyes were wide and her mouth parted and she spoke in barely a whisper, “What is this song?”

He didn’t understand the sudden change in her mood until the song’s name came to him, “It’s Zelda’s Lullaby. It’s a traditional royal family song. It was played for the Princess as a child to lure her to sleep.” 

Her eyes gleamed with tears, her jaw tight as she stared at him, “I know this song” she said breathlessly. “My mother used to play it for me as a child.”

It was obvious she was doing everything to not break in front of him. The song was about to end, “Do you want to get some fresh air?”

She stared out past his shoulder in a trance. Then seemingly snapped out of it and shook her head, one rouge tear fell down her cheek and she tried to blink away the rest. “No. I’m alright.” The song had ended and she quickly pulled her hand from his to wipe the tear away. She smiled weakly at him and returned to their table where Fledge and Groose still sat.

Thoughts swirled of Purah’s comment from yesterday, the evidence she was of royal blood continued to mount. Her own mother played her Zelda’s Lullaby, in whatever realm she came from. Too many coincidences continued to occur. Too many to be ignored.

As he made his way to the table, she had already wiped the tears away and was smiling at Fledge. As if the past few minutes never happened. She swigged the rest of her drink and was calling for another.

The rest of the night passed without mention of the song. Zelda continued to drink and be merry as if she had never heard it at all. Then she asked Fledge to dance, making him deeply uncomfortable as he shot Link a silent plea for help. Link shrugged, suppressing a smile as Zelda dragged the quiet, nervous man out to the dance floor. 

Link watched as she urged him to grab her waist, his face growing as red as a tomato.

His thoughts were interrupted by Groose’s baritone voice, “She likes to have fun.”

The band was playing another jig, a popular poem made into a song. Zelda was twirling, her skirt extending as her feet bounced and stomped to the beat as Fledge tried to keep up with her charged energy. It was entertaining to watch his friend flounder, but watching Zelda be so free and happy was another. 

He forgot Groose had spoken to him, finally acknowledging with a simple, “She does.” If he was trying to hide his longing from Groose, he was failing miserably. He swiftly changed the subject, “You mentioned it’s going well with the Princess?”

Groose adjusted in his seat, “Yes, as good as expected.” He trailed off, uninterested in continuing that line of conversation. He shifted in his seat looking slightly anxious as he opened his mouth to continue, “I’ve wanted to apologize for what happened at the tournament. I had no idea they were going to choose me over you. Of course, I’m honored, but you are clearly the better knight in every way. I was hoping to tell you months earlier, but I heard you were assigned shortly after.”

He looked to the giant knight with his ridiculous hair style, sincerity lined his features, “Groose, never apologize for that. Yes, at the time it was a bit jarring, but—” he couldn’t help but look at Zelda laughing brightly with Fledge as she accidentally stepped on his foot. “It all worked out for the best in the end.” And he meant every word of that.

As much as he tried to suppress it, he couldn’t. Groose gave him a knowing look as Fledge and Zelda made their way back to the table. Zelda laughing breathlessly and Fledge looking completely flustered.

She sat down next to Link and whispered in his ear, setting every hair on edge. “This might be our new hangout on weekend evenings. The new normal for us.” He swallowed tightly as she continued, “Since I’m probably never going home.”

She was drunk. Slurring her words.

She shook her head, and Fledge took notice of their conversation as she whisper-yelled. “Impa will realize soon enough. She’ll kick me out of the castle, and I’ll have to find a way to work. I could be a barmaid here, I suppose.” She continued to drink as Link was paralyzed to speak, unsure if he should stop her or let her go.

Now she looked at Fledge. “Or I guess I can try to marry someone here, right? That’s all women seem to be able to trade for. I’ll find a husband who can take care of me while I tend to the house.” She rolled her eyes. “Perhaps the bard can take me traveling with him.” She pointed to where the bard was still playing. “Or Purlo will stash me away at the outpost while he pretends to guard!” She barked out a laugh and quickly covered it with her hand.

Link was stunned by her drunken outburst. And that mentioning Purlo in that context didn’t bother him as it normally would. Instead, he felt such sadness for her that she had seemingly given up and resolved to a life she never imagined or wanted.

It was time to go.

“Come on, Zelda. It’s late. We should go back. We need to leave tomorrow.”

She narrowed her eyes at him, brows drawn down, questioning his intentions. “Okay. Sir, honorable knight. I shall go where you go.” She slurred and waved her hand to gesture to nothing.

He snaked his hand around her waist innocently to keep her from falling as she tripped over her chair getting up. She looked so vulnerable as she tried to straighten herself. He threw a quick nod at Fledge and Groose as they smiled and nodded their goodbyes to Zelda, and she waved at them.

They made the long trek to their apartments. She was oddly quiet the whole way, except for her ragged breathing. He opened her apartment door and realized he would need to help her all the way inside.

He’d only ever seen her room through their shared door. He imagined being in here under different circumstances often, but certainly not as she was now. He ushered her to her bed, and she sank onto the mattress, her eyelids growing heavy, then closed. Her clothes and shoes remained on, and while he would never dare remove her clothing without her conscious consent, he would take off her muddy shoes before she slipped under the covers.

He kneeled before her and delicately untied each boot and set them down near the foot of her bed, noticing the chest of clothes open at the foot of her bed. He eyed the familiar white dress he had first found her in; that memory skittered through his spine at the thought of the similar situation now, yet so incredibly different months later.

“Link—?”

Had that been his name she mumbled? He turned back to her. Her eyes still closed. “Zelda?”

She curled into herself and turned to face the wall, her golden blonde hair somewhat loose from her braid behind her. Perhaps imagining her mumbling, he turned his back to her and started to leave.

“You’re so hands—. —perfect. —lucky to be with.” She mumbled, barely audible as he couldn’t make out all the words as she slipped into unconsciousness.

And perhaps she would remember in the morning, he didn’t care if she did, but he leaned down, swept the rest of her silken golden hair from her face and kissed her temple. “Goodnight, Zelda. I’m so thankful you came into my life.”

Chapter 22: Water
Chapter Text
She had an unholy ache in her head.

She awoke the next morning feeling dreadful. In her bed but still in her clothes from the night before.

It took her a minute to register where she was, as she stared at the familiar gauzy fabric in the canopy of her bed. Then she remembered the tavern, Fledge and Groose, the bard, dancing. Then things started to get hazy.

She vaguely recalled dancing with Link, with Fledge. She remembered a song, a familiar song. The cold walk back slightly sobering her as Link held her upright. He laid her into bed and took off her shoes, or perhaps she did. 

A knock on her apartment door had her shuffling her socked feet to open it. Link brought her breakfast, a quiet yet smug smile on his face as he noticed her disheveled appearance, still in her clothes from the night before. They were supposed to leave this morning for Zora’s Domain, the final region she had yet to visit, but he took a glance at her and asked if she would prefer to spend the day resting. To her relief, she agreed. If she had to be honest with herself, she probably would have fallen off of Storm if she tried.

As she shut her door on him, not able to stomach having him look at her in this state, she placed the delicious yet nauseating-looking food on her desk. She breathed through her mouth thinking about how she wanted to ask Link what happened, but on the other hand, not knowing might be better. She couldn’t bear how embarrassing she probably had been.

She spent the entire day in her room, piecing together the events of the prior night. Regretting drinking too much until her throbbing head ceased. She noticed that one thing that remained consistent from home was the fact that Hyrule ale gave her the same hangover as ale from home.

She wasn’t a drinker at home, except for occasional indulgences during dinner or nights out. She had had a few drinks in Hyrule, but something unleashed her last night; she craved to lose control. Purah and Robbie’s words echoed in her subconscious, the ominous forces at bay, the sinking feeling of never returning home, and incidentally, the possibility of returning home.

Link and she had been getting along quite well, actually. He flirted with her, and she flirted with him. She did remember complimenting his dancing and how he offered to indulge her curiosity about all his impressive skills, anytime she desired.

The way he said it made her shiver, her core going molten.

Could she be so bold to advance on him that way? Her growing desire for him was becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. Scattered fragments of memories of him dipping her, his breath tickling her jaw, her hand pressing on his hard chest, and his piercing blue eyes made it hard to breathe when she looked into them.

She cursed herself again for drinking too much. Had she not, she could replay his words, analyze his gaze in vivid detail. How she wanted to decipher it, explore it.

Would anyone mind if they decided to have a more physical relationship? It would be easy to conceal their actions since they had adjoining doors in a completely empty building. He could touch her anywhere, and she could loudly cry his name in ecstasy. She could even make the first move; she had no qualms doing that.

But she was in a different place with different rules. Rules she didn’t fully understand yet. The last thing she wanted was to embarrass herself further by mistaking his chivalry for interest.

She slipped into her bath, which was gradually easing the last of her nausea, and tried to melt away the lingering shame.

It had been a few days of traveling now towards Zora’s Domain. She could see the moonstone arches and buildings in the distance, all set against a quarry of glowing, mountainous rocks.

Link had not brought up anything she had said or done at the tavern; he was ever the gentleman. They continued their pleasant conversations and camped as they went. Link’s sleeping arrangements were not hindered by the rain, and with no excuse to invite him into her tent again, they slept in their traditional arrangements, which perhaps had been a good thing. As much as she secretly hoped otherwise.

As they followed the winding path of the Zora River, he gave her an education on Zora’s Domain, the Zora people, and his personal history with them.

The Zora race were an aquatic species, possessing both human and amphibian-like traits, including fins, webbed feet, and the ability to breathe underwater and above it. They are the only other race in Hyrule that is considered royalty and respected as such, having a King, Princess, and Prince. Link had grown up with Princess Mipha, as his father was stationed in Zora’s Domain for a brief time. Link was fond of Mipha, looking at her like a sister; she taught him how to swim, and he taught her how to use a bow.

There was a small part of her that was nervous, meeting someone who Link considered the closest thing to family he had left.

Crossing an ethereal moonstone bridge, she was hit with the scents of the rich earth and water’s tangy minerals. The feeling of childlike wonder spread throughout her senses as the mountains around them seemed to breathe in response, glowing pieces scattered around them. The landscape complemented the delicate architecture, probably not by coincidence. Everything was elegantly designed, with attention to craftsmanship evident throughout. A faint blue glow seemed to emanate from all directions, setting it apart from all the other regions’ capital cities she had visited.

Two guards stood at either side and nodded to Link in silent recognition. They were as Link described, finned humanoids that towered over them both. They had long tails cascading down their backs from their heads, similar to dolphins. They were magnificent; their skin glittered in the bright sun, causing her to stare a bit too long.

“The architecture in Zora’s Domain glows from luminous stones; it’s a rare gem that can be found in ore deposits.” Link whispered to her, as if reading her mind, as they crossed the bridge’s canopy.

Ironically, she felt like a fish out of water being here. In her plain, dull-colored travel attire surrounded by the clean, decadence of this palace. Even Link looked at ease, with his red tunic against the pale, glass-like stone— he was relaxed. Suited to it. She stepped quietly next to him, carefully observing her movements.

They continued walking to what she assumed was the main plaza. Staircases were on either side of them, either leading to the second level or twisting into private balconies. There had even been a shrine right in the middle of it all. She scowled at the unforgiving, cold stone emitting that bright orange glow that brought back negative memories.

She snapped out of it as a soft melodic voice called out, “Link!”

They turned their direction to the staircase on the right. A small, red-finned woman was walking down to greet them.

As she stepped closer, Zelda saw that she was small, shorter than them both. She was dripping in jewelry, from her silver headpiece all the way down to her ankles. All encased in silver and adorned with various gems and symbols. Like the Gorons, she was not wearing traditional clothing but rather a belt swept across her chest.

Her eyes were piercing yellow, like molten gold, complemented to her coloring. They darted from Link to Zelda and back to Link again.

She, without hesitation, brought Link into a warm, loving embrace. “Link, it’s been so long!” Her calming voice had said as she pulled back from him.

“It has. I believe it was the Summer Ball we last saw each other?” He said with a cocked brow. She nodded slowly, regally.

“A lot has changed since then.” Link turned to face Zelda, implying she was the ‘A lot that has changed.’ His expression was neutral but satisfied as the woman scanned her, taking her in from foot to head, tilting her head, in a curious way. “Princess Mipha, this is Zelda.”

Zelda promptly bowed and did a crass curtsy, “It’s my honor, Princess.” She was unsure how to greet royalty because she never had to curtsy in her life. Mipha laughed wholeheartedly.

“Please, no need for formalities, call me Mipha. It’s lovely to meet you, Zelda.” Her voice sounded like rainbows and the warm rays after a rainstorm. Mipha promptly closed the distance between them and pulled her into a hug. Zelda suddenly felt relaxed and eased by the friendly gesture.

Mipha turned back to Link. “I hope your trip was smooth. Not too much rain?”

“Actually, no rain, oddly enough for the time of year.” Zelda was sure Link’s tone wasn’t implying anything untoward.

“Lovely. I did receive your letter a few days ago from the emissary Impa sent. I understand she has sent you both here to find answers on Zelda’s sudden appearance here in Hyrule. My father is out but will be receiving guests tomorrow. Since it’s already late in the day, I can show you to your chambers, and we can join for supper afterwards?”

“That sounds great. Thank you.” Zelda replied with a shy smile.

Mipha led them to the inn. An enclosed space decorated with the soft glow of luminous stone and carved moons in various phases. Windows and arches left the room completely open to the elements. Zelda supposed that given they were an aquatic species, the rain probably didn’t bother them as it would humans.

There were two beds side by side, out in the open. No curtains for privacy.

She wouldn’t dare be rude to ask for a more private residence. It wasn’t that she minded sleeping so close to Link, considering the recent turn of events. But where would she change or get ready for her day? She turned to Link, her face unavoidably tight. He looked at her with a knowing look.

“Thank you, Mipha. But do you have the foldable dividers somewhere nearby?”

“Ah, right. I’m sorry, I forgot Hylians preferred privacy.” Mipha walked to the closet on the side of the room and pulled out a folded divider, similar to the one she had in her castle apartment by her bathroom.

She didn’t consider herself a prude and honestly, she thought about seeing Link’s glorious naked form more often now-a-days, but she did draw the line at being completely exposed to anyone walking by.

“I’ll let you two freshen up? Meet you in an hour?”

Linked nodded, “Thanks, Mipha.” And she smiled as she turned away, gliding out of the inn with preternatural grace.

Zelda flopped on the farther bed from the inn’s entrance, knowing Link would insist on taking the closer one to the entrance. It started to wave her whole body— a water bed. She couldn’t hide the pure amusement that painted her features. “I should have guessed it would be a water bed.”

Link shrugged with a smile, “It’s not so bad. I prefer to sleep on hard surfaces myself, but it feels sort of like floating.”

She tried to maneuver herself to face him, but the bed was making her body look ridiculous, “Is this where you stayed as a child?”

“Yes, my father and I.”

“What did you and your father do while you were here, besides what you’ve already told me?” Which had been very little.

Link tensed his jaw as he quickly looked out at the open window above his bed.

Just because they shared a moment together a week ago, didn’t necessarily mean he was open to sharing every aspect of his past. He walked to his own bed, first taking his sheathed sword off and sat on the jiggly bed facing her. Zelda opened her mouth to object, but Link started first.

“I was young, maybe seven the first time I came here. My father was a knight, but he wasn’t from nobility. Most of the knights you see and know come from noble families, so he had to work extremely hard to get to that position, and he earned it off of pure merit alone. When he met my mother, he opted to derail his career in favor of settling down with her. He could have stayed at the castle, become a royal guard, but he chose love and asked for leave so they could move to Hateno Village, where they had me shortly after.”

He started to remove his bracer and continued, “When I was young, he was sent out on lousy assignments, the captains somewhat punishing him for choosing a family over a promising career. Until King Dorephan, Mipha’s father, needed help one year with monster control. He specifically asked for my father, knowing his reputation from his years at court. So he came and was treated like family by the Zora. The next year, they had a similar issue and summoned him again specifically. The king and my father became close and struck up a friendship, then each season, my father would visit and handle various jobs for them. Then I started attending with him as well.”

“Is that how you and Mipha became close?”

“Yes, she was born decades before I was, but the Zora age slower than us, essentially she’s our age. We became fast friends, just as her father and mine had.”

“Sounds like fate.” She said while sitting up with a watery smile. Matching the bed, swishing in motion.

He was unbuckling his shoulder guard, “Yes, perhaps. But she’s easy to love.”

“Thank you for the lovely compliment, Sir Link. I would have to say the same about you.” Mipha had quietly entered their space with rosy cheeks and a warm smile.

“I only say the truth, Princess.” He stripped off the last of his guards and set them down, next to his sword. 

“Dinner is ready. If you’d both like to follow me.”

Mipha escorted them out and onto the second floor, to a more secluded area with pools. A long table was set up near the edge, covered with large platters of food, trays, and drinks, as if designed for hosting royalty. 

“Is this all for us?” Zelda asked sheepishly.

“Yes, of course. I wasn’t sure how much you would eat, but I surely know Link’s appetite could manage this no problem.” She shot him a coy smile.

Link rolled his eyes.

They sat and savored their seafood-based meal. The fish was so flaky and light, perfectly battered, and accompanied by a decadent buttery sauce. Sides of wild mushrooms and herbs, paella with mussels and clams, and even caviar were piled high on serving plates. Link and Mipha spent the meal catching up, as if no time had passed while Zelda listened intently. The conversation flowed effortlessly and she noticed how relaxed Link had become, any knightly strain wiped from the fibers of his body.

By the time the meal was over, she had never eaten so much or so well in her life.

Mipha escorted them back and said her good nights. Zelda had been so full by the time she changed into her nightclothes that she lay in her bed in defeat. With only a salty, light breeze kissing her cheeks and the sounds of the water flowing all around them, her eyes became heavy as the silken sheets and the motion of the bed rocked her to sleep.

The next morning she awoke, somehow still full. Link was already gone as she glanced to his empty bed. She wondered how far he would have to go to train here to avoid accidentally cutting or maiming someone.

She took the opportunity to be lazy in preparing for the day; she splashed water on her face and changed into a flowing dress to take advantage of the warmer, humid climate. It was a bright blue, matching the water and architecture all around her. But not the same blue as Link’s eyes. Nothing ever was.

She stood in front of a gilded mirror as she finished brushing her hair, deciding whether to leave it down in its natural state, at the mercy of the humidity, or tie it back when she noticed Mipha entering the room.

“Good morning, Zelda.” Mipha said cheerfully. She was dressed in all her finery befit a princess.

“Good morning, Princess.” 

“Please call me Mipha.” She smiled warmly. She walked towards her and stood behind her, her eyes meeting her own in the mirror. “Would you like to join me for breakfast?”

“I would love to.” Zelda turned from the mirror’s gaze and followed Mipha to the second story. 

Another table was set up in the same location, again with enough food for twenty. This time covered in breads, pastries, fruit, spreads, and cheeses. Any assumptions Zelda had of the Zora people’s diet had vanished.

“Shall we wait for Link?” Zelda looked to Mipha earnestly, not wanting to break any traditions she may not be aware of.

“He won’t be joining us. He ate early this morning and went to the Veiled Falls to train.” 

Zelda tried to hide her surprise but it was odd. Link never missed breakfast, nor left her alone when they traveled. He must have trusted Mipha wholeheartedly.

Mipha sat and insisted she dig in, so she did. She would not let this amazing food go to waste.

After getting settled with a few bites, Mipha asked in between sips from an elegant teacup, “May I ask you a question?” Zelda nodded, swallowing an abnormally large bite of a breakfast bread as Mipha continued, “I know Link was assigned to you, but how did you two meet before that?”

Zelda recounted her story to Mipha, “He found me when I appeared inside the castle walls. He took care of me, sheltered me, and fed me all before his tournament. Master Impa must have felt that since he already knew and helped me, he should be the one leading me around Hyrule for answers.”

Mipha listened intently, now taking a delicate bite of a pastry. “How interesting. I’m quite shocked that they didn’t choose him to guard the Princess. I mean no offense.”

Zelda feigned surprise but quickly faded to curious contemplation, “Not at all. From what I hear, that’s what everyone says.”

An awkward silence fell between them, but Zelda pushed to know more. “You knew Link as a child?”

“Yes.” Her smile reached her eyes, “He and his father would come to the Domain together. I remember him being such a reckless child. Always getting hurt and roughhousing. But I would always be willing to heal him.” Mipha stared at her plate, recounting the fond memories.

“Heal him?” Zelda asked, giving her a puzzled look.

“I have healing abilities.” Mipha raised her hand as if to show Zelda an invisible power laying beneath. “I can heal cuts, gashes, and even more serious wounds. But there are limits, sometimes there are injuries too severe for anyone to heal.” 

Zelda’s jaw dropped. “That’s incredible! I’ve never seen or heard of anything so amazing. What a gift.” She couldn’t contain her girlish excitement. Out of all the magic and mysteries Hyrule had to offer, healing someone was at the top of that list.

Mipha blushed, “I have been very blessed. Perhaps I was given this gift specifically to heal Link.” She giggled. “So as he grew, small cuts from sticks and stones grew to larger ones from swords and arrows.”

“I can’t imagine Link as a child but I can imagine him needing the healing—” Zelda trailed, searching for the right word, “—since he’s quite— brave.”

Mipha nodded her head in agreement, “As he grew, his focus on training did as well. The older he got, the more dedicated he became. He continued to visit every summer until he became a page.” She turned her head to one of the bridges leading out of the palace, to where Link possibly was. “Now I’m lucky to see him once or twice a year.”

She sounded sad at that admission. “He mentioned you come to the castle a few times a year?”

“Yes, we are invited to royal family gatherings. Since he’s become a knight, I only see him on those occasions. I just wished perhaps he would make the effort to visit the Domain. I know it’s selfish since he’s so busy.” Mipha forced a weak smile.

“It’s not,” Zelda said quickly. “It’s never selfish to wish to see family or friends more often.”

Mipha gave her a warm look, “Before I received his letter, I had been hoping he would visit. I have a surprise for him, and I need to get his measurements.”

“A surprise?” Zelda cocked her head in an inquisitive look.

“More like a gift, custom Zora armor tailored specifically to him. It will enhance his swimming in water.”

“I’m sure he’ll love that.”

Mipha blushed, “But please don’t tell him. I want it to be a surprise.”

“I wouldn’t think of it,” Zelda said and smiled so fondly at perhaps another that she could call a friend here in Hyrule.

Link had made it back, his hair completely wet when he strode into the inn. He had decided to take a plunge in the pond he’d been training in after becoming sweaty. Zelda eyed his dry clothes inquisitively, to which he replied he’d gone in completely commando, and Zelda had to force every ounce of her composure not to react, despite the heat of her core rising to her face.

Mipha had arrived after to usher them to the meeting with her father. 

As they followed behind Mipha up to the mysterious third floor. Zelda couldn’t miss the large Zora sitting in front of them. The King had to be as tall as two stories and almost as wide. He was blue in color, unlike his daughter’s red coloring. He had wrinkles near his eyes that surely showed his age to those that knew how to read it. Zelda wondered if Mipha would grow to be that large someday, if perhaps their slow aging also applied to their height.

Mipha petered off to the right where another Zora sat, this one was a child, much smaller than Mipha but the same coloring as her.

When they stopped in front of the King, Zelda followed Link’s lead who knelt while she curtsied. 

“Father, this is Zelda, Link’s charge. Zelda, this is my father, King Dorephan.” Mipha said, “and this is Prince Sidon, my brother.” She waved her hand to the small Zora child who smiled an impressive toothy smile in greeting at hearing his own name.

“A pleasure to meet you, dear Zelda.” The King said with a voice that boomed and echoed in the chamber it nearly knocked her over, “And Link, my boy, always a pleasure to see you.” He said, his eyes twinkling. He was overjoyed at seeing the knight by her side.

“You as well, King Dorephan, thank you for receiving us.”

“Anything you need. We will always welcome you, and your guests. So tell me what is going on.”

Link handed him the letter sealed from Impa, the last of the four. The King read it thoroughly and Link recounted the past five months to him including every clue or whisper they’d come to learn.

The king was quiet for a good while, processing all that Link had said. He eyed Zelda intensely, but not suspiciously. Then he leaned forward in his seat and spoke, “The Hero of Time. Very interesting. Our ancestors helped the hero in his task. Actually, it was rumored that Princess Ruto was betrothed to him.” Mipha noticeably fidgeted next to her father. “The rumor goes that as a child, he asked for the Spiritual Stone, the Zora Sapphire, but the Princess would not give it to him, as it was special to her, meant to be a symbol of her betrothal. He then rescued her, and with that, she gave him the stone willingly. It was said he used it with the other two to open the Door of Time.”

“Spiritual Stones?” Link parroted back.

“Yes, precious, sacred stones that were used by the hero. Each stone embodied the very spirit of courage, power, and wisdom, respectively. The Kokiri, Goron’s, and Zora all had one each, gifted to their people to protect. The young hero was brave and faced down each threat in their regions, in turn they gifted him their respective stone as thanks. With the guidance of the young Princess Zelda, he needed to present all three stones at the Temple of Time, which opened the door to the Sacred Realm. With the door open, the Master Sword presented itself to him, but he was too young to wield it, so the Realm sealed him away. Inadvertently traveling through time, in a way.” The king finished his long-breathed explanation and narrowed his eyes at Zelda. “Not quite like you, my dear, but I see why this story might lead to a clue.” He then turned to Link. “I’m surprised you don’t know this story, my boy.”

Link started, “I do know the story of Hero of Time and of the Master Sword. Impa mentioned stones but never called them Spiritual. Do you know where the Zora Sapphire is now?”

The king barked a laugh that shook the walls. “Oh, my boy, those were lost to time, if they ever existed at all. It was so long ago, you know how record-keeping goes with scholars.”

Link hadn’t replied. Zelda looked sidelong at him. A stoic, blank expression laid upon his features.

Did he silently curse every time they gained more information, that only led to more questions? He seemed particularly bothered that the Spiritual Stones were lost to myth; it just meant the longer he’d have to stay with her. Five months ago, Zelda would have cried at the redirection, but now, the longer it took, she hadn’t minded. She had been enjoying every moment, the new scenery in every region, every new race of people she met, and savoring all the emotions flooding back to her she thought long dead.

She nervously ran her fingers through her hair. Trying not to let her shoulders cave in on themselves in front of the king.

The king shrugged, his eyes warmly crinkling. “Don’t be discouraged, I’m sure your Master Impa will have more information for you both. In the meantime, you are both very welcome guests here in the Domain. We shall feast tonight, and you may stay as long as you wish.”

“Thank you, King Dorephan,” Link bowed.

“Yes, thank you for your hospitality, King Dorephan.” Zelda mirrored with a head bow and curtsy.

“Thank you, father. I’ll walk them out.” Mipha led them down the staircase.

As they reached the bottom of the staircase, Mipha stopped. “Zelda, do you mind if I steal Link away for a moment?”

“Oh— Of course,” Zelda nodded her agreement, trying to hide the dazed look on her face.

“Thank you, you are welcome to explore anywhere you wish in the domain. We shouldn’t be long.”

“Are you sure you’re okay on your own for a bit?” Link finished his sentence with his jaw clenched, and she could see the muscle visibly twitch.

“Yeah, I’m okay. I promise I won’t leave the Domain,” she gave him a small knowing look, “take your time.”

Link gave her a small nod, Mipha smiled and they split off to the east bridge together. Zelda walked down the stairs alone, resolved to find something to entertain herself for the rest of the day.

She decided to read. It had been so long since she let herself fall into the pleasure of a story. She hadn’t been able to indulge in her preferred romantasy genre, but she managed to find volumes of legendary stories from the castle library. And she couldn’t help but swoon over the hero’s actions.

The weather had been perfectly sunny and warm, so she decided to spend the day outside. She walked around each level of the domain, admiring the elegant architecture and stonework, looking for the perfect place to read. She watched as young Zoras splashed and played in the pools, poking the shells of snails in disgust and screaming as they ran away. Then she noticed a Zora woman attending to an article of clothing. Zelda decided to stick her feet into the pool and politely watch from a distance before cracking open her book.

The woman was hand sewing on scales to an unfamiliar water-wicking material. The tunic was as blue as the water beneath her feet and adorned with silver-plated armor and jewels. Zelda marveled at the intricate handwork that was going into the material, it had to have taken her countless hours to assemble.

Zelda couldn’t tear her eyes away from the craftsmanship, until she heard, “It’s for my paramour.” The Zora woman said, startling Zelda.

“I— I’m—sorry to be a distraction. I’ll leave you to it.” She had been so enthralled by the needlework that Zelda hadn’t noticed she had become enthralled at the Zora. She started to pull one foot out of the water.

“I don’t mind. It’s nice to have a distraction.” The Zora woman said without lifting her head from her work.

“It’s a gorgeous piece. Is it a gift?”

“Yes… in a way. It’s our tradition here. Female Zora craft an armored tunic for their beloved when ready for marriage. We craft it by hand and present it to them. If they accept, the couple is then considered to be engaged.”

“What a charming tradition…” Zelda trailed off. “Does your paramour know?”

“We’ve spoken about it.” She continued to thread a scale onto the chest piece, “We’ve been together for years. He knows it’s coming, just not when.” 

What a nice tradition, Zelda thought. In her culture, engagement rings were given, but an exquisite tunic could be nice too and practical. Zelda thanked the woman for the explanation and got up to leave, making her way to the first level. It was well after lunch, and she was hungry. She would perhaps find something to eat near the market—

Wait.

It hit her like a lightning bolt. She gripped the balcony tightly as she was descending the stairs, stopping in her tracks. 

Mipha had said that morning that she needed Link’s measurements for a custom tunic.

Could it be? She had planned to propose to him?

The air felt heavy, or perhaps breathing had become difficult. 

Is that what she’s doing now? Measuring him and telling him about the tunic? Have they spoken of engagements and plans for their future?

An older Zora snarled at her as she continued to stay frozen midway down the stairs. She resumed her walking, straight into the inn. 

When she got the semi-privacy she needed, she crashed on her bed, slapping aggressively against the jiggling mattress. Her head was spinning. 

Mipha wouldn’t go through all the trouble of creating something so significant without having a pretty good idea that Link would agree. Link had never mentioned anything beyond his childhood friendship with Mipha. In fact, she recalled him mentioning that it had been a while since they last met.

But would he ever tell her if he was in a relationship with her?

She felt a pang of hurt cross her heart as she breathed deep, pushing it down and away.

He said to her in the desert, “No woman who has pursued me has interested me,” but that left it open that he had pursued others. Perhaps he intentionally left it ambiguous to torment her, or perhaps he wanted to keep it from her.

But he flirted with her. Danced with her, in a way that couldn’t be only friendly… that couldn’t have been her imagination. But Cole flirted with other women while he dated her. Hell, he cheated on her.

But Link didn’t come across that way. Sure, she didn’t expect Cole to cheat, but he wasn’t a good man. Link was a good man; he wouldn’t—

But just because they were together all the time and getting along didn’t mean he had to tell her everything about his life, nor did she expect him to.

She breathed in the sharp, crisp air. Smelling of citrus and floral sweetness. Her head spun. She was suddenly overwhelmed by the realization that her presence was hindering his ability to engage in simple activities, such as meeting friends or forming a romantic relationship. It hadn’t crossed her mind until now.

If he had been in a relationship or desired one, her constant presence over the past few months would undoubtedly push it to the back burner, but it wouldn’t necessarily extinguish it entirely. Could it be that he had other aspirations in life before she arrived, but they were now impossible to pursue until she was gone and home? He himself expressed regret for not seeing Mipha in quite some time. What else was he missing out on due to her presence?

“Zelda?”

Zelda sat up quickly, completely caught off guard. Link was standing in the doorway, alone. His brows were narrowed in concern; she probably looked mad. She scanned him for a scaled blue tunic, on him or in hand, but luckily he was in his familiar red one, except his bracer was off. Mipha couldn’t have finished it. She had mentioned this morning that she needed measurements. Perhaps he had removed his shirt to allow her to take more accurate—

“Zelda, are you okay?” He interrupted her spiraling.

She let out an exaggerated breath. “Yeah… sorry.” How embarrassing. She hadn’t replied to him the first time, instead glaring at him with eyes as large as the moon.

She watched him carefully as he walked over to the desk and placed the bracer down and started to unbuckle the rest of his guards, setting his sword down next to him.

“How was your time with Mipha?” She managed to choke out.

He hadn’t bothered to look at her when he answered, “It was nice to catch up with her.”

“What did you two do?” She hadn’t meant to sound so suspicious, hoping she hadn’t come across as possessive.

“We went on a walk to the cliffs’ edge, sat and had a conversation about youth and what we’ve both been up to since we last saw each other.” He still hadn’t met her eyes.

She was slightly relieved at no mention of tunics or measurements. But perhaps he omitted it. She had to remember he was not entitled to tell her everything. 

“How was your afternoon?” He asked as he finished removing the last of his guards. “I see you managed to stay out of trouble.” A handsome smirk painting his face. She almost melted at the sight, but remembered he could be a taken man, she had to treat him as such.

“It was good… spent time admiring the architecture and spoke with some locals.”

“Learn anything good?”

She swallowed. “Indeed I did.”

She was quiet throughout the rest of the night. They had dinner together with Mipha, Sidon, and the King. Zelda couldn’t help but notice Mipha’s loving gazes towards Link while she thought no one was watching. She observed if Link reciprocated her feelings, but as expected, he remained the epitome of a knight, maintaining decorum and propriety in front of the King.

How had she not seen it sooner?

The next morning, Link was up before dawn. This time, Zelda heard and saw him wake, yet did not say a word. She had been tossing and turning all night, tormented by the inconvenience she had caused him and his life. After he left, she rose and watched the sun rise from her window as she dressed and readied herself for the day.

Link met them all for breakfast, the same trio from dinner, including the King, who said his farewells as he planned to leave for a trip to a nearby village shortly after breakfast. He specifically warned Link not to be a stranger with a wink, and Zelda couldn’t help but harbor negative thoughts about how well Link already blended in with Mipha’s family.

She hated herself for that. This was not who she was.

After breakfast, a guard came to Mipha and whispered about a threat on Ploymus Mountain. Link’s demeanor immediately stiffened at the threat, prompting him to push the guard for more information. A lynel was there.

The same beast they encountered weeks ago. Zelda’s eyes went wide at the horrid memories of the beasts and the one that almost killed Link. Killed her.

Mipha started to march off to go herself until Link said he would handle it. Mipha angrily insisted she come along, but Link asked her to instead stay with Zelda. He gave her a tense look in insistence until she relented and reluctantly agreed. 

Link shot Zelda a reassuring glance before departing, knowing the horrors of that day she witnessed and the near-fatal blow he sustained. All Zelda could manage to utter was, “Be careful.” As he shot her a faint smile and a nod. She watched as he walked over the east bridge to trek up the mountain.

“Come, let’s distract ourselves. I’ll grab Sidon, and we’ll go to Mikau Lake while we wait.” Mipha gave Zelda a small squeeze on her arm, and she instantly felt better. She wondered if her healing powers extended to internal worries and wounds.

As Zelda sat on the lake’s edge, soaking in another day of sunshine and warm weather, Mipha was teaching Sidon how to climb the cascading waterfall. Against the roar of the water, she watched the green frogs jump from lily pads and various fish swim against the current. There were so many scents weaving around her: florals, fish, grass, herbs, and… pine. She instinctively looked up past the waterfall, sensing his presence and wondering how Link was faring against one of those horrid creatures. She hoped more hadn’t come to ambush him as they did before.

“He’ll be okay. Link is the best fighter in all of Hyrule.” Mipha said in her melodic voice as she sat next to Zelda on the rock face.

“I know he will, it’s just— we faced this beast before and it almost ended badly.”

“I know, he told me, had it not been for you, he wouldn’t be here.” Mipha’s large golden eyes were soft and comforting.

“He told you that?” Zelda’s eyes widened at that truth Link provided her.

“Yes, he told me about the wound he received, how you threw a wooden sword at the beast—” Mipha chuckled at the idea of it, “—distracting it from it’s killing blow. Then, he mentioned how scared he’d been in that moment, the terror he felt when the lynel pulled out its bow and arrow to aim at you. It gave him the strength to push harder.” Mipha’s voice wavered ever so slightly.

“I was terrified I was going to watch him die, I couldn’t let that happen.” Zelda said as she stared at her closed palms, “I’m not that brave.”

Mipha grabbed Zelda’s hand, and a warmth flowed through her, creeping through her joints, spreading, blooming in her. As if a warm blanket laid over her and tucked her in.

Mipha must have sensed the unease and was lending her healing powers to her once more. She spoke softly, “I wouldn’t say that. You’ve endured so much since arriving here, and I can’t even begin to imagine myself in your shoes. It’s incredibly brave of you.”

Zelda never felt brave. She did feel free, though. Free to breathe, safe, and protected.

Protected.

And before she could fully articulate what she wanted to say, she blurted out, “Because Link has always been there, he’s been with me every step of the way. He’s saved me countless times, not just from monsters.” Zelda pursed her lips to simmer herself, “I don’t know where I’d be without him. I just want him to be happy. I know it’s his duty to protect me, but I don’t want to hinder his ability to have a life.”

Zelda felt light at the omission, despite being so frank about a man that may be in a relationship to the person next to her. She did truly mean what she said. She wanted him to be happy. With or without her.

Mipha smiled, her eyes large and sad. “I’ve known Link a long time. He’s always been serious about his military career. After what happened with his family, when he became a page and moved to the castle, he changed. He became solemn and stoic. It is a great honor to be a knight and a royal guard, and for years, that was all he focused on becoming. When I heard he hadn’t been assigned to Princess Zelda, I was shocked but grateful in a way. He always deserved more than being a mindless guard in my opinion. And now, he smiles again. He speaks more frankly. He makes jokes. It’s because of you.”

Zelda looked so deeply into Mipha’s eyes. To gauge any hint of deception or flattery. All that was there was honesty. Honesty that clearly tortured Mipha. Happy that her friend and/or boyfriend was happy, but perhaps a sadness that another woman made him that way.

Zelda instinctively shook her head at the comment. “No. He’s a royal guard technically. Impa made him one when he swore to me. He’s probably happy because he achieved his dream.”

Mipha’s brows pulled down flat, furrowing her center. Her mouth tight in a straight line as she shook her head, “No, Zelda.” Was all she said.

Zelda decidedly did not reply, unsure of what to say in this situation, until Mipha continued.

“If Impa, Link, or someone finds a way for you to go home tomorrow, would you go?”

Zelda’s mouth fell open then shut again. Unsure how to answer. Months ago, her immediate answer would have been yes, without question, but now…

“I don’t know.”

And that was the truth. It washed over her like a bucket of ice cold water.

Chapter 23: Knowledge

They’re already written; I just need a bit of time to polish them up. And if the name of this part gives you any clue about what’s coming for these two… well, you’ll see soon enough.

Chapter Text
Part 3 | The Precipice

 

When this is all over, perhaps we could spend some time together.

When this is all over.

He watched as a bee buzzed by, landing on the delicate pink flower next to him. The weight of the creature caused the stem to sway.

He was distracted.

He placed his sword tip down on the cobblestone and rubbed the bridge of his nose, inhaling the florals of spring.

He had been in the garden beneath their apartments since before the sun rose, trying— and failing, to focus on training. He impulsively kept glancing at Zelda’s balcony.

They’d been back at the castle since the night before. But Zelda had been quiet the whole trip back from Zora’s Domain. Hesitant.

Her distance and Mipha’s words were rolling around in his head. Zelda’s distance bothered him, but it was Mipha’s words that brought him pause.

When she spoke to him, back at the Domain, it had been in the privacy of the East Reservoir Lake. The night before that, he had asked her if she could heal the lingering lynel wound he had received. He didn’t necessarily want to hide it from Zelda, but he didn’t want her to be concerned. Mipha had happily agreed, explaining that she wanted to speak with him privately anyway.

As they sat overlooking the lake, he rolled up his sleeve and she began the magic of her healing on his forearm.

Perhaps it was the flood of joyful memories from his youth that had bubbled to the surface from the past day. Or perhaps the lush grass, the refreshing water, and the invigorating air all contributed to a sense of lightness and tranquility, momentarily easing his tension, but he was uncharacteristically loose-lipped with his old friend.
